concepts.def: Three-cell model (Hadley, Ferrel, Polar) driven by uneven heating; explains belts of high/low pressure and prevailing winds.
Tropical circulation: warm air rises at equator (low pressure, rainforests), descends at 30 degrees (high pressure, deserts).
Apparent deflection of moving air due to Earth's rotation; right in Northern Hemisphere, left in Southern.
Intertropical Convergence Zone where trade winds meet near equator; band of heavy convectional rainfall, migrates seasonally.
Caused when warm air meets cold air at a front; warm air rises, cools, condenses; typical of UK depressions.
Local variation in climate over small area due to factors like aspect, urban heat island, water bodies or vegetation.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Weather Hazards & Climate Change — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Weather Hazards & Climate Change brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Weather Hazards & Climate Change.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which cell brings rainfall to the equator?
Where does the ITCZ migrate seasonally?

numericals.q: At what latitude (degrees) do deserts form due to descending air?

free_texts.q: Name the effect deflecting winds due to Earth's rotation.
